findings.description: The R5a/R5b outcome expression at line 170 tests `within ±0.05` before it tests `c.get("insufficient")`, so a contrast whose valid-cell count is below the pre-registered threshold but whose interval happens to sit inside the band is labelled `within ±0.05` instead of `insufficient`. The R5 aggregation at line 176 has the same ordering problem: `the model explains the lift` / `the gates earn their cost` are assigned before the `insufficient` check, so an insufficient R5a paired with a within-band R5b yields a definitive branch. The generic `outcome()` function gets this right (insufficiency first); the R5 path does not. The current rows (Σ5 cells on R5) are not affected, but the script is the pre-registered decision instrument and the report plans re-runs.
findings.failure_mode: On a re-run where one R5 cell drops out (e.g. an r18 arm loses a trial to contamination), the script can print a definitive R5 branch from a read that the pre-registration defines as insufficient, and the JSON `reads.R5.outcome` carries that wrong branch into the DEC rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Route R5a/R5b through the same precondition as `outcome()`: `"insufficient" if c.get("insufficient") or not c.get("ci90") else ("within ±0.05" if ... else "outside ±0.05")`. In the R5 aggregation, check `"insufficient" in (R5a, R5b)` first and return `insufficient` before evaluating the two definitive branches.

findings.description: `grade_of` swallows every exception and returns None, and `s3_eligible` (lines 61-72) returns False on any exception. Neither emits a warning, and the report has no column saying how many grades or transcripts were actually found. When `--batches-root` lacks the batch directories (they live on the record branch, not with `c131-rows.jsonl`), the `diff_only` sensitivity silently falls back to row-level `oracle_exposed_defects` and the S3 sensitivity silently becomes identical to `trial_level`, because no row can be S3-eligible. Likewise rows failing the pin check are kept in `rows`, counted in the title (`27 c131 rows`) and in the inventory `rows` column, but silently dropped from every read.
findings.failure_mode: Anyone reproducing the formal read from the main branch gets a `c131-reads.md` whose S3 table differs from the published one (a1_full r18 shows 2/3 instead of 3/3) with no indication that inputs were missing; the discrepancy looks like a data change rather than a missing-input condition.
findings.suggested_fix: Count missing `grade.json` files and unreadable transcripts and either abort or print a prominent line in the report header (`grades found N/27, transcripts found M`). Add a `pin_ok` column to the row inventory, or drop pin-failing rows in `load_rows` with a logged count.

findings.description: The run directory is derived as `r["run_id"].split(f"-{r['arm']}-", 1)[1]` with `r["batch"]` and `r["arm"]` accessed by subscript. In `grade_of` this happens outside the `try`, and it is executed for every row at load time (line 151). `load_rows` admits a row when either `batch` or `run_id` starts with `c131-`, so a row with a `run_id` prefix but no `batch` key, or a `run_id` that does not embed `-<arm>-`, is admitted and then raises KeyError/IndexError, aborting the whole run before any table is produced. The same expression is duplicated in `s3_eligible` (line 63) where it is at least inside the `try`.
findings.failure_mode: One malformed or differently-formatted row in a future rows file (e.g. a resumed cell written with a different run_id scheme) crashes the formal read with a traceback instead of excluding the row.
findings.suggested_fix: Factor a `run_dir(r, root)` helper that uses `.get`, checks the separator is present, and returns None otherwise; have `grade_of` and `s3_eligible` both call it and treat None as missing. Better, have the batch scanner write an explicit `run_dir` field into each row.

findings.description: `caught_set` builds the defect universe as `{d1..dn}` from the manifest's defect count and subtracts `defects_missed_pm3`. The manifests are loaded in `main` (line 150) but only `len(...)` is used; the actual defect ids are never read and there is no check that every entry in `defects_missed_pm3` is a member of the universe. Any id that does not match the `d<i>` form (different casing, zero-padding, a renamed defect in a future manifest, or a grader that emits names) is silently ignored, which counts that defect as caught.
findings.failure_mode: A grader or manifest id-format change inflates `defect_catch_rate_pm3` for the affected arm without any error, biasing a contrast in the direction of whichever arm's grades were emitted in the new form.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the universe from the manifest (`{d["id"] for d in manifest["defects"]}`), pass it instead of `n`, and raise or warn when `set(missed) - universe` is non-empty.

findings.description: CHANGELOG (KF-051) and analysis.md §10.7 state that Fable-refusal rows "read degraded and are excluded from model contrasts". In the script, the R5 specs (lines 158-159) exclude only rows where `fallback(r)` is true, i.e. where some `phases[].refusal_fallbacks` list is non-empty. The `degraded` flag is consulted only in the `strict` sensitivity (line 49), not in the main R5 read. If a KF-051 row records the fallback via `degraded: true` (or under a different key than `phases[].refusal_fallbacks`), it is included in the headline R5 contrast, contrary to the documented exclusion. The current rows show 0 degraded and 0 fallback so no number changes.
findings.failure_mode: A future batch containing a KF-051 row that is flagged `degraded` but whose fallback is not recorded exactly as `phases[].refusal_fallbacks` enters the bare-Fable vs full/bare-Opus comparison, contradicting the documented rule for the model read.
findings.suggested_fix: For the `exfb` specs exclude `r.get("degraded")` as well as `fallback(r)`, or make the row schema guarantee that every refusal fallback sets both, and say so in the valid() docstring.

findings.description: The docstring defines S3 eligibility as a row "whose only recorded hit is an outside_path write under a scratch directory". The implementation inspects a single `contaminated` dict (`pattern`, one `excerpt_id`) and one transcript line; it never verifies that there is no second hit. The scratch token `"/tmp/"` is a bare substring test, so any command mentioning a path such as `<repo>/tmp/` or `/var/tmp/` passes the shape check. Classification is otherwise fail-closed, which is good, but the implemented rule is looser than the pre-declared text in one direction (multiple hits) and than the intended path shapes in another.
findings.failure_mode: A contaminated row carrying an outside_path hit plus a second, more serious hit recorded in a sibling field would be re-included in S3, or a row whose command only touches a repo-internal `tmp/` directory would be classified as a scratch write.
findings.suggested_fix: If the contamination record has a hit list, require every hit to be `outside_path` with a scratch shape; otherwise document that the grader guarantees a single hit. Anchor scratch tokens to a path start (`$HOME/tmp/`, `/tmp/` preceded by a space, quote or `=`) rather than bare substring.

findings.description: The `strict` sensitivity drops any row with a non-empty `dissent_absent_gates`. For the `a1_no_dissent` arm the dissent is absent on every gate by design, so the filter removes the whole arm and R4 under `strict` prints `0 defects / r17:0/3 (Σ0) / None / insufficient` (visible in c131-reads.md). That row reads as an evidential result but is a construction artefact, and the text `insufficient under every read` in analysis.md §10.4 leans on it.
findings.failure_mode: A reader of the strict table takes the R4 `insufficient` as a fourth independent confirmation when it is the sensitivity excluding the arm it is meant to test.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the `dissent_absent_gates` criterion for arms whose toggles disable the dissent (or for reads where arm A is `a1_no_dissent`), or print `n/a (arm excluded by construction)` for R4 under strict.
